summary: NYPD Blue is a television police drama created by Steven Bochco and David Milch, inspired by Milch's relationship with former NYPD member Bill Clark, who later became a producer. The series aired on ABC, debuting September 21, 1993, and ending March 1, 2005. The note states it was ABC's longest-running primetime one-hour drama until Grey's Anatomy surpassed it in 2016.
one_line: NYPD Blue is a 1993–2005 ABC police drama created by Steven Bochco and David Milch, once ABC's longest-running primetime one-hour drama.
key_facts: NYPD Blue was created by Steven Bochco and David Milch.
The show was inspired by Milch's relationship with Bill Clark.
Bill Clark is a former member of the New York City Police Department who eventually became one of the show's producers.
The series was originally broadcast on the ABC network.
NYPD Blue aired its final episode on March 1, 2005.
NYPD Blue was ABC's longest-running primetime one-hour drama series.
NYPD Blue held the ABC longest-running primetime one-hour drama title until Grey's Anatomy surpassed it in 2016.
